::: {.callout-note}
## About this chapter
Most of this chapter draws on a single deep-research pass (`evidence/deep-research-report.md`)
that is heavily cited but **not yet independently verified claim-by-claim**. Treat
names, dates, and titles here as well-sourced leads rather than settled fact until
spot-checked against the primary documents it cites.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Four internal sources, four different framings of 1977 {#the-1977-conflict}
Both 2017 internal decks say the archive came under **ISSR** in 1977. The Dataverse
About page names Donald Treiman as the 1977 framework's designer with no
institutional home stated. A later book-chapter draft says the archive was created
in 1977 "as part of the **Survey Research Center**," no ISSR mention at all.
External evidence (UCLA's 1977–78 General Catalog, via the deep-research pass)
supports ISSR as the actual named parent, with SRC as a component under it. That
makes the book chapter's SRC-only framing the likeliest one to need correcting, but
confirm it against the catalog directly. Don't assume it. See
[Sources & Open Questions](sources.qmd).
:::

The archive's 37 years under this institutional umbrella break into three distinct
subperiods, not one continuous arrangement.

## ISSR proper (1977 – late 2000s)

An international directory published through the OECD describes the **ISSR Data
Archive at UCLA** as established in **December 1977** to support quantitative
research, "primarily secondary analysis." Data came mainly through UCLA's ICPSR
membership, supplemented by federal statistical agencies (Census Bureau, National
Center for Health Statistics, National Center for Education Statistics, Bureau of
Labor Statistics) and locally produced studies such as the **Los Angeles County
Social Survey**.

**Directors identified:**

| Director | Period | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Howard E. Freeman | Late 1970s – ~1980 (founding director) | High |
| Marilynn B. Brewer | 1983 (snapshot; exact term unknown) | High for 1983 |
| David O. Sears | 1993–2008 | Very high (per his own CV) |

**Operational staff identified** (roles tied to ISSR/SRC broadly, not all
confirmed as archive-specific): Eve Fielder (SRC director), Rita Engelhardt
(statistical services), Donald Witzke (sampling), Michael Greenwell (CATI
facility), Ann Cinderella and Madeleine/Madelyn De Maria (assistant directors),
Cheryl Groves and Kathleen O'Kane (coding supervision), Matthew Futterman and Jack
Katola (programming), Tana Wong (assistant director, 2009).

## Renamed: Institute for Social Research (~2009–2011)

By the 2009–10 UCLA General Catalog, the parent institute's name had changed to
the **Institute for Social Research (ISR)**: same phone number, new website
(`isr.ucla.edu`), same components, including the Social Science Data Archive. No
director has been identified for the institute under this name. The renamed
institute still appears in the 2010–11 catalog.

## Standalone SSDA (~2011–2014)

By the 2011–12 catalog, neither ISSR nor ISR appears as a named institute. The
**Social Science Data Archive** is listed independently, as a Social Sciences
collection, using its own website (`dataarchives.ss.ucla.edu`). No public source
identifies a formal dissolution date or a single institutional successor for the
parent institute.

Elizabeth "Libbie" Stephenson, the archive's head archivist and later director,
is the strongest through-line across this entire chapter. She started around
1977, the same year the archive became a named ISSR unit, and stayed through
the 2014 Library transfer, retiring in 2016. That means one person's tenure
spans essentially the whole ISSR era end to end, plus two more years. By the
early 2010s the archive was moving toward modern research-data curation
practice: a 2013 conference paper documents SSDA experimenting with the
DDI-Lifecycle metadata standard and Colectica curation software immediately
before the Library transfer. See [People](people.qmd) for her full career
profile and `evidence/stephenson-icpsr-sources.md` for sourcing.

## What's still unresolved

- The exact reporting line for SSDA between ISR's disappearance (~2011) and the
  2014 Library transfer.
- Who, if anyone, directed the renamed ISR (2009–2011).
- The formal date and authority for the ISSR-to-ISR rename, and for ISR's eventual
  dissolution.
- Whether digitized ISSR/SSDA newsletters exist anywhere outside the indexes
  checked so far: UCLA General Catalog, eScholarship, Internet Archive,
  HathiTrust, Google Books, UCLA Digital Library, none found. This is a
  negative search result, not proof none exist.
